headline: Supreme Court Clerk Accidentally Files Petition Demanding Apology for Forgotten Tiffin Box
body:
The Supreme Court of India was momentarily thrown into a state of confusion on Thursday after a junior judicial clerk accidentally processed a legal petition demanding a formal apology for a missing paneer-stuffed paratha. The filing, which was mistakenly registered under the docket for high-profile litigation, reportedly contained a detailed account of how the clerk’s lunch disappeared from the staff canteen refrigerator during the hearing of a major state appeal.

“The petition was extremely thorough,” noted one court stenographer, who spent two hours proofreading the clerk’s grievance. “It cited the Indian Penal Code, the law of torts, and even included a signed affidavit from the canteen manager confirming that the paratha was, in fact, prepared with extra ghee. It was formatted so professionally that the registry initially considered it a constitutional challenge before realizing it was just a lunch dispute.”

Chief Justice’s office officials confirmed that while the matter has been dismissed for lack of urgency, they are considering an internal inquiry into the canteen’s storage protocols. The clerk has since withdrawn the petition, reportedly satisfied after a Senior Advocate offered to share half of their cucumber sandwich during the tea break. The court has officially returned to its regular business of deciding the fate of the nation.
caption: When the legal system is so well-oiled that even a missing lunch gets a docket number. Justice served, one paratha at a time. #SupremeCourt #IndianLaw #CanteenCapers (satire)
